title: Rav Ada son of Rav Azza
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Kiddushin 81b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.81b.13), he speaks in the name of Rav Assi. Hyman considers it very likely that he came with all the travelers [from the Land of Israel] in Abaye’s time, and he is the one mentioned in [Temurah 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Temurah.21a.6-11): “Rava son of Rav Azza said: They asked in the West — Abaye said to him.” He conjectures that it was written רב״א, an abbreviation for Rav Ada. Hyman reports that Yuchasin names Rav Acha son of Rav Azza and has the difficult words אמר רב אביי. Hyman reads them as “Abaye said to him.”

notes.text: The entry’s subject reports Rav Assi; the opening does not merely quote Rav Assi as an unrelated speaker. Saved Davidson Kiddushin 81b has Ada bar Rav Azza/Avva, and Temurah 21a has Rava bar Rav Azza and an alternative Acha reading. Hyman’s travelers inference, abbreviation reconstruction and Abaye correction remain qualified; the father-name variant is not erased.

[Temurah 21a:6–11](https://www.sefaria.org/Temurah.21a.6-11) preserves two versions of the exchange with Abaye. The first names Rava son of Rav Azza, and the second names Rav Acha son of Rav Azza and reverses which case is asked first.
